ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Act on Reporting and Use of Certain Financial Transaction Information (as last amended), its Presidential Enforcement Decree and the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit Beneficial Owner Identification Regulations; Act on Regulation and Punishment of Concealment of Criminal Proceeds (as last amended); Act on Prohibition of Financing of Terrorism and Proliferation of Weapons of Mass Destruction (as last amended); Real Name Financial Transactions and Guarantee of Confidentiality Act (as last amended); Commercial Act; Non-Contentious Case Litigation Procedure Act; and the applicable Supreme Court registration rules. The Republic of Korea maintains no public UBO register; beneficial ownership information is collected by financial institutions and designated non-financial businesses and reported to the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit under a government-only access model.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation / Company Registry Extract of the foreign investing entity and the Korean Chusik Hoesa
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Supreme Court Registry Office of the Republic of Korea or the competent corporate registry in the investor's jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: If issued in Korea: certified extract by the Registry Office, notarization by a Korean notary, and Apostille by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea under the Hague Apostille Convention. If issued in a non-Hague state: certification by the issuing registry, authentication by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the country of origin, and subsequent consular legalization by the Embassy or Consulate of the Republic of Korea in that state; the Apostille route and the consular route are parallel and mutually exclusive and are never stacked sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of No Judicial Dissolution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Supreme Court of Korea, for the Korean entity, or the competent company registry of the foreign investor's home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For Hague member states: notarization plus Apostille issued by the designated competent Apostille authority of the country of origin. For non-member states: notarization, foreign ministry authentication, and consular legalization by the Korean diplomatic mission exercising jurisdiction over the origin; the two authentication paths are mutually exclusive.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution / Power of Attorney appointing the resident director, representative, and authorized signatories for incorporation and bank account opening
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors of the investing corporate shareholder, certified by a notary public in the jurisdiction of execution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: The executed resolution must be notarized and translated into Korean. If the execution jurisdiction is an Apostille state: Apostille by the designated competent authority. If not: legalization by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the execution state and then consular legalization by the Korean Embassy or Consulate; use only the path applicable to the jurisdiction of execution.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association (Chusik Hoesa deed of incorporation, prepared in Korean with an English translation)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Founding shareholders and a Korean notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: The notarized Korean statute must be apostilled by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea if it will be used outside Korea; for any foreign-language certified copy, the foreign notary or authority must use either Apostille if the origin is a Hague member, or Korean consular legalization if the origin is not a member, before acceptance by Korean courts or banks.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter / Certificate of Good Financial Standing from the investor's existing bank
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing licensed commercial bank, with letterhead, original wet signature and unambiguous authorized signatory capacity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: The bank letter must be notarized or certified by the bank's registered signatory, then either apostilled by the domestic competent authority if the bank's country is an Apostille Convention member, or authenticated by the foreign ministry and legalized by the Korean Embassy or Consulate if the bank's country is not an Apostille member; dual-path use is prohibited.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copies of passport / identity cards, proof of residential address and criminal record clearance certificates for each director and ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public of the document holder's country of residence; Korean Mission if issued abroad
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Each notarial certificate must be apostilled by the competent authority of the Hague member state where the notary is located, or legalized through the Korean consulate when the notary is located in a non-member state; Korean domestic documents require notarization and MOFA apostille through the local court.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All shareholders, directors, ultimate beneficial owners at the 25% threshold, authorized signatories and high-risk counterparties must be screened before incorporation, at director changes, and continuously during the relationship. The screening matrix must include the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, the UN Security Council Consolidated List, the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, Korean FIU-designated listed persons, Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Korea Customs Service restrictive financial measures, and domestic criminal and regulatory disqualification registers. Enhanced due diligence must verify domestic and foreign PEP status, including prominent public officials, immediate family members, close associates, state-owned enterprise leadership rank, adverse media, sanctions exposure, beneficial ownership chains, source of funds and source of wealth; suspicious transactions must be reported to KoFIU as an STR within three business days. The screening tool must be automated, auditable and retained for at least five years after termination of the relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Office (I-RO) name search and corporate registry; National Tax Service Hometax business registration interface for post-incorporation business name registration
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The statutory registered name of a Chusik Hoesa must be in Hangul and clearly include the corporate form suffix indicating a stock corporation. An English transliteration may be registered as a parallel trade name provided it is consistent with the Hangul name and does not create confusion with an existing registered name. The four-tier naming convention is: a distinctive proprietary element, a business-activities descriptor, the corporate-form suffix, and an optional English parallel trade name for payment rails and customs invoices. Korean registration authorities require a name-search certificate showing the absence of identical names and prohibit names likely to mislead third parties regarding false governmental affiliation, financial institution status, or medical claims.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the I-RO name-search or the registration officer rejects the proposed name, the applicant must obtain a written rejection specifying the conflicting name or prohibited token. The applicant may then file an objection with the registration judge of the competent district court under the Non-Contentious Case Litigation Procedure Act within 14 days from the date of rejection, attaching the rejection notice and a corrected name search. If the court confirms the rejection, the applicant may appeal to the High Court; where an administrative authority under Hometax or local government denied the business registration, the applicant must file an administrative appeal to the Tax Tribunal within 90 days and, if necessary, institute an administrative suit within 90 days. Before each re-filing, a fresh I-RO name search must be conducted and the reservation window restarted; a reservation cannot be tacitly extended, and an administrative decision restoring the name is retroactive to the date of the original filing.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For a South Korean Chusik Hoesa engaged in online cross-border sales of nutraceutical supplements, the Ministry of Food and Drug Safety expects a real operating site with the ability to control document storage, labeling, recalls and returns. The National Tax Service and commercial banks reject a pure virtual office or commercial mailbox as a registered address for high-risk merchant account and VAT compliance purposes; such an arrangement will almost certainly trigger enhanced document requests and field inspection. A licensed serviced office with a dedicated physical suite, lease agreement, signage, staffed working area and accessible filing and deed room may be tolerated only during the pre-incorporation stage, but before the health functional food business report and high-risk merchant account are obtained, a conventional full-term office lease or an actual operational location in Korea is required.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Likelihood: HIGH, conservatively estimated at more than 60% within the first 18 months of operation. Mandatory checklist for inspection readiness: physical registered office with unlocked and staffed premises; exterior signage matching the Korean legal name; original lease certificate and utility bills; business filing cabinets with VAT invoices and customs records; employment records; local inventory or controlled storage area; evidence of actual management substance; compliant health functional food labeling; records of consumer complaint handling; and a named on-site officer. Municipal tax offices, local public health centers and the National Tax Service may carry out unannounced visits, especially for e-commerce food and supplement businesses with high revenue volatility and first-year VAT refund claims.
