incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of South Korea, Act No. 1000, enacted December 31, 1962, as most recently amended; specifically Articles 289 (incorporation), 290 (subscribers and stock subscription), 295 (payment of share subscriptions), 301 (incorporation meeting), 305 (officers appointment), 317 (registration of incorporation), and 318 (legal effect of incorporation), together with the Rules of Registration under the Commercial Act (Corporate Registration Rules) and the Act on Promotion of Information Technology Utilization for the Court System for electronic filing procedures.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Company Registration Office of the Local District Court (Beobindeunggi-so) within the judicial district in which the registered head office is situated, operating under the Supreme Court Registration Administrative Affairs Office; in Seoul, the Seoul Central District Court Company Registration Division.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Chusik Hoesa statutory Incorporation Registration Application (Chusik Hoesa Seongnip Deunggi Sinhcheongseo) together with the certified Articles of Incorporation (Jeong-gwan), the Stock Subscription Report (Jusik Insu Bogos), the Minutes of the Incorporation Meeting (Changlib Chucho Uisagirok), the Subscription Deposit Certificate, and proof of officers' acceptance of office.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. The amended Commercial Act does not impose any mandatory minimum paid-up capital for a general Chusik Hoesa; the founding share capital may be fixed at any positive amount, and no blocked escrow account obligation exists by statute. The only procedural safeguard is the requirement that the aggregate subscription proceeds be fully deposited into a nominal bank account established in the name of the company at a Korean commercial bank or securities depository institution prior to the convening of the incorporation meeting. The subscribed amount must be paid in cash or, if the articles so permit, in kind with an independent inspector's valuation report. Cross-border subscription payments must conform to the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and be evidenced by a Korean bank remittance certificate.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS RESOLUTION
OF [●] CHUSIK HOESA, A STOCK CORPORATION

RESOLVED, THAT the incorporation of the company under the Commercial Act of South Korea is hereby accepted, and the proposed statutory Articles of Incorporation filed for corporate registration with the Office of the Court Registry are ratified, approved, and confirmed as the constitutive charter of the company.

RESOLVED, FURTHER, THAT all subscriptions to the company's common shares, having been lawfully offered, subscribed, and paid in full by the subscribers named in the Stock Subscription Report, are hereby accepted and certified, and that the deposit certificate issued by [●] Bank evidencing the receipt of the aggregate subscription price in the incorporation deposit account is ordered to be archived in the permanent corporate records.

RESOLVED, FURTHER, THAT the registered office and principal place of business of the company shall be and hereby is established and located at [●], the address set forth in the certified Articles of Incorporation, and the Representative Director is instructed to sign, execute, and file the incorporation registration and to procure the physical posting of a company sign and the registration of the office lease in the appropriate municipal and tax records.

RESOLVED, FURTHER, THAT [●] Bank, having its principal office in Korea, is designated as the principal corporate banker of the company, and the Representative Director and Chief Executive Officer are, jointly and severally with the Chief Financial Officer, expressly authorized to open, maintain, and operate all demand deposit, settlement, foreign currency, online trading, merchant processing, and risk-managed payment gateways, to execute account-related mandates, to appoint signing and approval authorities within the enterprise banking interface, and to instruct the bank on payment orders, transfers, high-risk merchant acquiring, credit card settlement contracts, and any overdraft or trade finance facilities that the board may from time to time approve.

RESOLVED, FURTHER, THAT the following natural persons are herewith appointed as the statutory officers of the company, each to hold office until the next ordinary general meeting of shareholders and until their successors are lawfully elected: [●] as Representative Director and Chief Executive Officer, [●] as Director of Operations and [●] as Director of Finance, and [●] as Statutory Auditor where such officer is required by law; each such officer having delivered an unconditional acceptance of appointment and a declaration of compliance with Articles 382 and 542-2 of the Commercial Act.

RESOLVED, FURTHER, THAT the common seal of the company and the official seal of the Representative Director shall be produced, registered at the competent Court Registry, and used in accordance with corporate seal management policy under the Registered Seal and Corporate Documentation Act.

RESOLVED, FURTHER, THAT the officers of the company are ordered to complete the business registration with the National Tax Service, the health-functional-food sales registration under the Health Functional Foods Act, any cross-border e-commerce permits, and the fire safety and environmental operational certificates, and to take all actions necessary to carry these resolutions into full effect, including the payment of all filing fees and taxes associated therewith.

RESOLVED, THAT the acts of any officer taken before this resolution are hereby ratified as acts of the company where done in furtherance of its incorporation and operation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarial Certification and Execution of the Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Certified Notary Public licensed under the Notary Public Act of the Republic of Korea, operating at the territorial notarial office of the promoter or, in the case of foreign promoters, the Korean Embassy or Consulate notarial service.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The promoters must prepare and execute a statutory instrument titled Articles of Incorporation containing the corporate name (Chusik Hoesa), the precise business purpose of online retail of dietary supplements and nutraceuticals, the registered office address, the classes and number of shares, the par value per share, the total issued share capital, the annual general meeting provisions, the officer election method, and the standards for financial statements. Every page of the articles is required to be serial-numbered and stamped or signed by each promoter. The executed articles must then be submitted to a certified notary who verifies the identity, contractual capacity, and purpose legality of all signatories, confirms that mandatory Commercial Act provisions are present, and issues a notarial certificate of solemn promulgation. Where a foreign promoter is involved, a notarized apostille/apostilled power of attorney should be submitted into the record. The authenticated instrument is the foundation of all later registry filings and must be retained without alteration.
required_dossiers: Passport or valid national ID of each promoter
Original signed Articles of Incorporation on numbered legal paper
Notarization instruction letter to the Korean notary public
Proof of registered office address (lease registration certificate or written consent of premises owner)
Name availability ticket issued by the court registration information system
Apostilled power of attorney for foreign promoters
Legal capacity certificate for corporate promoters (certificate of incorporation of direct parent) if any
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: In the event the notary issues a defect notice, the promoters must amend the defective article clause, re-execute the affected pages, and resubmit the full instrument for a fresh notarial certification within one business day; notarial fees are retained for actual work performed, but minor drafting corrections are usually remedied without additional charge. If the notary raises a legal feasibility objection regarding the business scope, the promoters may narrow the purpose clause and resubmit with a legal memorandum.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Establishment of the Incorporation Deposit Account and Payment of Subscribed Share Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Enterprise Banking Centre of a licensed Korean commercial bank (e.g., Shinhan, Woori, Kookmin, Hana) or a licensed securities brokerage institution authorized to hold incorporation deposits; for cross-border funding, the foreign exchange operations of the bank under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The promoters must approach the designated deposit institution and open a dedicated incorporation deposit account in the name of the company being formed. For each subscriber a formal Stock Subscription Form (jusik insu jung) must be executed indicating the number of shares and the amount payable. After the subscription records are collected, each subscriber must wire or remit the full subscription amount into the incorporation deposit account. For Korean residents, a simple account transfer suffices; for non-resident subscribers, the remittance must be reported at KEB/Shinhan’s foreign exchange desk and a Foreign Remittance Certificate must be obtained. The bank must issue a certificate of deposit in the legal name of the company reflecting the aggregate paid-in amount, which certificate is the statutory proof of paid-in capital for the later court registration. The institution must retain the company’s prospective business registration number and the promoter’s identity records for compliance and then return a ready-to-file deposit certificate.
required_dossiers: Fully completed Stock Subscription Forms for every subscriber
Initialled bank account opening application in the corporate name
Certificate of deposit or deposit account statement issued by the bank
Foreign exchange transfer receipt for any non-Korean funding
Subscriber identity documents and source of funds declaration
Authorization letter from the promoter appointing the bank as deposit agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any wire transfer is delayed or blocked by foreign exchange supervision, the depository bank shall issue an acknowledgement of pending remittance, and the amendment may be extended by one additional business day; if a subscriber default occurs, the promoters may declare the subscription void and reissue a new share allotment, provided the aggregate paid-in capital remains at or above the amount stated in the articles, and the deposit certificate will be corrected by the bank with a new issue date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Convening and Holding the Statutory Incorporation Meeting and Election of Officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Promoters' assembly acting under Articles 301 and 305 of the Commercial Act; the assembly is an internal statutory body but minutes may be certified by the notary for evidentiary effect.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The founders and all subscribers are required to convene the statutory incorporation meeting before the expiration of the agreed date for subscription payment. The meeting is attended in person or by proxy, with a packed agenda comprising: (i) verification of paid-in capital and stock subscription forms; (ii) approval of the promoters' report and any incorporation-inspection report prepared by a court-appointed inspector; (iii) adoption of the final text of the Articles of Incorporation; and (iv) appointment of the initial board of directors and statutory auditor, if required. Each director-elect must deliver an acceptance of office and provide a statement that they are not subject to disqualification under Article 542-2. The minutes must be signed by the chairman of the meeting and at least one witness, and a notarized summary extract is recommended when foreign directors are elected. After the meeting, the minutes and resolutions are written into the corporate minute book and signed by the representative director.
required_dossiers: Solemn notice of the incorporation meeting with attendance list
Original or notarized proxy forms for attending subscribers
Minutes of the Incorporation Meeting signed and witnessed
Stock Subscription Report signed by each subscriber
Certificate of deposit or paid-in capital repository certificate
Directors' and auditor's written acceptance of appointment
Notarized company seal imprint if prepared
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the meeting is formally challenged for lack of quorum or incorrect notice, a second corrective meeting may be convened with a shortened 24-hour notice, and the prior defective minutes are to be declared null and void; any statutory inspection deficiency must be cured by applying to the reasonable court for appointment of an inspector before the registration step.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Application for Incorporation Registration at the Local District Court Company Registration Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company Registration Office (Beobindeunggi-so) of the District Court that has territorial jurisdiction over the registered head office; for Seoul, the Seoul Central District Court Company Registration Division.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within two weeks from the day following the incorporation meeting, the Representative Director or an authorized agent must submit the application for incorporation registration to the competent court registry. The prescribed form is available on the electronic court filing system or at the registry counter. Documents must be assembled in the statutory order: (1) the certified Articles of Incorporation; (2) the minutes of the incorporation meeting; (3) the stock subscription and inspectors' report; (4) the deposit certificate; (5) the notices of election of directors and auditor; and (6) the acceptance of office forms. The registry officer will verify the legitimacy of the incorporation, the sufficiency of the paid-in capital proof, the statutory form of the articles, and the legal validity of the business purpose. Upon successful examination, the registry enters the company into the commercial register and issues a Certificate of Registration (registration completion certificate), which is the conclusive evidence of the company's legal existence and effective legal personality.
required_dossiers: Fully completed statutory Incorporation Registration Application
Notarized certified Articles of Incorporation in one original and one copy
Minutes of the incorporation meeting and attachments
Stock subscription report
Certificate of subscription proceeds deposited into the incorporation account
Inspectors' report covering non-cash contributions (where applicable)
Letters of acceptance of office for all directors and auditor
Registered seal specimen, if separate seal registration is performed
Power of attorney in original if filed through legal counsel
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry raises a formal defect notice, the filer must respond within three business days by supplying the requested supplementation or correcting the compliant document. If a substantive defect is identified, the application may be withdrawn and re-filed with rectified documentation, with the original filing fee being credited against the re-filing. If the application is rejected entirely, the promoters can appeal the decision to the court or bring a civil remedy, but the customary remedy is to resubmit promptly after curing the defect, while ensuring the deposit certificate remains valid and the incorporation meeting is recertified if necessary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business Registration with the National Tax Service and Corporate Seal Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) branch office with territorial jurisdiction over the company's registered place of business; the Circuit Court notarial registry for the issuance of the corporate seal certificate.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within twenty days following the date of incorporation registration, the Representative Director must file an application for Business Registration (saupja deungrok) with the relevant local tax office. The application must designate the major business category as 'retail sale via mail order or internet of health functional foods and dietary supplements' (ISIC 4791) and separately list the online shopping mall and the physical warehouse address if different. The director must supply the unique business number, corporate certificate, lease documentation, and the bank account details for VAT administration. Simultaneously, the corporate seal and the representative director's seal must be filed at the District Court registry and a certificate of corporate seal impression must be obtained. After issuance of the Business Registration Certificate and seal certificate, the company must open one or more operating bank accounts and register for electronic tax invoices. The final package of registration and license certificates is kept in a compliance folder for review by the cross-border acquirer and regulatory authorities.
required_dossiers: Business Registration Application (NTS Form on the HomeTax system)
Certificate of Incorporation entry from the District Court registry
Corporate seal certificate and ordinary seal imprint
Registered office lease agreement and utility bill
Bank account designation details for taxation
Director passport and corporate representative ID copy
Application for electronic tax invoice issuance
Health functional food sales business registration filed separately at the Gu office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the NTS delays issuance pending the e-tax invoice or additional tax classification, the company should request interim processing and attach an explanation addressed to the head of the tax office. If the corporate seal certificate is refused, the board may adopt a corrective resolution, re-record the seal specimen, and submit an updated registration within one week. All adverse determinations may be appealed administratively through the National Tax Service Administrative Appeals Division under the Taxpayers' Rights Charter.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Food and Drug Safety (MFDS) supervised licensing channel in cooperation with the competent Gu District Office (Health and Food Administration Division) where the registered online retail office and any ancillary storage are located; for e-commerce platform duties, the Korean Fair Trade Commission (KFTC) under the Act on Consumer Protection in Electronic Commerce.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Health Functional Foods Sales Business Registration (건강기능식품판매업 신고) under Article 5 of the Health Functional Foods Act and the E-Commerce Business Operator Report pursuant to Article 12 of the Act on Consumer Protection in Electronic Commerce; for foreign-source dietary supplements, an Imported Food Business Registration under the Special Act on Imported Food Safety Control is also required by the MFDS if the company itself imports and sells to cross-border consumers.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment and the local Gu District environmental office under the Environmental Impact Assessment Act (EIA Act), Article 42 administrative authority for unlisted small projects.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable - Exempt. The business is an online retail operation with no physical manufacturing, chemical processing, assembly line, or warehouse exceeding environmental threshold; the activity falls outside the mandatory EIA project categories, and a full Environmental Impact Assessment is not required. If the company in the future establishes a warehouse larger than 10,000 square meters or adds any packaging or chemical handling, the EIA classification will be rechecked and a formal Screening / Preliminary Environmental Review under Article 43 of the EIA Act may become required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable for the permitted retail activity because there is no process wastewater, no VOC emitting process, no hazardous chemical storage, and no hazardous waste generation. The leased office and small local stockroom must nevertheless comply with municipal wastewater sewer discharge limits generally (BOD below 300 mg/L for commercial premises), local atmospheric nuisance laws for heating systems (sulfur oxide limit of 0.03 ppm at boundary and particulate matter at 100 mg/m3), and must arrange separate waste collection and recycling under the Wastes Control Act. Any future e-fulfilment warehouse will need to observe the Standard Discharge Permit Approach for industrial wastewater of the Ministry of Environment, including a total volatile organic compound discharge limit of 600 mg/L for any solvent-based waste and regular disposal contract for any contaminated packaging materials.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate (Anjeon Jeomgeom) issued by the local District Fire Department under the Fire Services Act is required for the registered office and any storage space, demonstrating operation of detectors, extinguishers, and evacuation signage; a Civil Defense Shelter exemption is assumed unless floors exceed 720 square meters. In addition, the workplace must obtain a general workplace safety clearance through the Korea Occupational Safety and Health Agency (KOSHA) under the Occupational Safety and Health Act, including a manual handling risk assessment for boxes of supplements, emergency exit plans, and electrical safety certification for any battery-operated equipment; the fire and safety inspection certificates must be posted in each workplace of the company and exhibited to the inspecting authorities.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea, with electronic filing via HomeTax (www.hometax.go.kr)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Korean Chusik Hoesa (stock corporation), the company must register with the local district tax office within 20 days of incorporation to obtain a Business Registration Number (BRN), which serves as both the TIN and VAT ID. The application requires the articles of incorporation, certificate of incorporation, proof of registered address, and identification of the legal representative. For foreign non-resident entities without a domestic establishment, a simplified VAT registration is available under the VAT Act for suppliers of digital services to Korean consumers, requiring a foreign business registration number, a Korean tax representative, and a domestic address for service of process.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None (no check-the-box elections; group taxation election available for qualifying parent-subsidiary groups but not applicable to a single entity)

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: KRW 0 (mandatory registration for all domestic entities)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory electronic tax invoices (e-invoices) via the NTS HomeTax system for all B2B transactions; real-time transmission to NTS; anti-fraud measures include digital signature and validation; B2C transactions require cash receipts for consumer purchases.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods are zero-rated under Article 21 of the VAT Act. For e-commerce, goods sold to foreign consumers and delivered outside Korea qualify for zero-rating. Qualifying offshore digital services supplied to non-residents are also zero-rated.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Bill of Lading or Airway Bill
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Penalties include additional VAT of up to 40% of the underpaid amount, plus criminal charges and imprisonment for fraud. Retrospective clawback of zero-rating benefits with interest is enforced by the NTS.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) in coordination with the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) and the Financial Services Commission (FSC)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea operates a broadly liberalized convertibility regime under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and the Foreign Investment Promotion Act. Current account transactions, including trade payments and ordinary service fees, are freely convertible with no central bank approval; banks merely verify the underlying trade document and prescribe transaction purpose codes for FEIS reporting. Capital account transactions are general-market-convertible but require notification, declaration, or approval depending on event type. For a Chusik Hoesa receiving foreign direct investment, the non-resident investor must file a foreign investment notification with a Korean foreign exchange bank or the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy before advancing equity capital, and the funds must be deposited in a foreign currency deposit account. There is no mandatory exchange surrender for inward investment or export earnings, but every receipt above USD 10,000-equivalent must be traceable to a bank report. Profit remittance via dividend distribution is allowed after corporate tax settlement and is not subject to a separate remittance cap; the bank will verify corporate tax payment certificates and the withholding tax payment record. Transfer pricing, tax clearance and beneficial ownership paperwork are the practical hurdles, not convertibility restrictions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No mandatory conversion ratio is imposed under Korean law; exporters may retain export proceeds in foreign currency, and no surrender to the central bank is required. The statutory requirement is that export proceeds must be collected through a prescribed payment method and physically received within six months from the export declaration date; an extension may be granted only by the MOEF/Bank of Korea for justifiable causes. All export proceeds must be reported to the responsible foreign exchange bank, and any uncollected balance after six months must be explained in writing. If the proceeds are received in a domestic foreign currency deposit account, they can be freely converted to Korean won without tax or penalty as long as the underlying export declaration and Invoice and Packing List are on file.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Currency Account
Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Currency Account
Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Currency Account
Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Currency Account
Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Currency Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-Barred for Primary Banking. In South Korea, only commercial banks and licensed internet banks such as Kakaobank and Toss Bank may lawfully accept deposits and hold operating funds of corporations under the Korean Banking Act. Offshore fintech EMIs and digital payment providers such as Airwallex, Payoneer or Currenxie do not have Korean banking licenses, cannot provide a domestic KRW IBAN, and cannot be used as the obligor structure for import/export settlement or capital escrow. They also cannot act as a substitute for a local FX bank account for FEIS reporting or foreign investment verification. The firm may use such an EMI only as an auxiliary offshore collection and disbursement overlay for ecommerce sales in smaller payment corridors, provided the main corporate account is maintained at a licensed Korean bank. FSS regulations treat unlicensed cross-border money transmitters as illegal when they serve local entities without an Electronic Money Transmitter license.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Even though Korea permits remote non-face-to-face account opening under certain FSC rules, a high-risk ISIC 4791 nutraceutical ecommerce structure is ordinarily escalated. The bank underwriting committee will require at least one statutory director, representative, or designated compliance officer to attend a physical branch interview before the account is activated. A purely consular-proxy opening with apostilled Power of Attorney is insufficient for the capital escrow account and trade facilities. For the initial account setup, the Korean statutory director(s) should attend in-person at the chosen bank’s headquarters or major corporate branch; remote video interviews may be used only as a supplement. The bank may waive the on-site mandate for the digital operational / collection account if a Korean resident compliance officer is appointed, but the AML team will likely require the subsidiary’s ultimate beneficial owner to be present at least once.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-Risk Jurisdiction Exposure: Ultimate beneficial owners are tax residents of jurisdictions on FATF Enhanced Follow-Up lists, or there is a contradiction between the UBO’s passport, tax residence, and bank reference.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: For every individual with 10% or more equity, submit a certified passport copy, national ID, CRS tax-residency certificate or letter from the competent tax authority, overseas bank statement from a FATF member country, source-of-wealth affidavit with notarization and apostille, and a professional reference from a licensed accountant or attorney. For each intermediate legal entity, supply the corporate registry abstracts, register of directors, register of shareholders, and a chain-of-control organizational chart covering the preceding five years.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Nutraceutical and Pharmaceutical Trigger: The imported supplements contain active-function ingredients, are advertised with disease prevention claims, or have not been notified to the Ministry of Food and Drug Safety (MFDS) as functional food.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the MFDS import notification receipt for each SKU, the Korean domestic functional-food establishment/business registration, HACCP or GMP quality certificates, Certificate of Analysis for every supplied batch, ingredient declaration and alloy/product specification sheets, labeling compliance review with a Korean attorney’s opinion, overseas supplier’s trading license, and product liability insurance naming the Korean entity as an insured party.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ecommerce Transaction and Payment Flow Anomaly: Large volumes of consumer card payments are expected but the underwriting package does not explain settlement timing, PCI compliance, consumer refund schemes, or use of aggregated PSPs for the online store.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver a 12-month revenue projection with average order value, refund/cancellation policy, card-acquiring contracts, PCI-DSS compliance certificate, website platform registration, domain ownership proof, hosting and privacy policy, formal AML manual with transaction monitoring currencies and threshold rules, and a process map showing how settlement funds are funneled from the gateway to the Korean company bank account.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial Ownership Opacity: The Chusik Hoesa has bearer-like shares, nominee shareholders, or unknown legal owners hidden through a chain of shelf companies in tax-neutral jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current registry extract issued by the Korean court, shareholders ledger, articles of incorporation, certificate confirming no bearer shares, sworn written statements from each shareholder that no nominee or trust arrangement exists, constitutional documents of any shareholders that are trusts/foundations, and a signature letter from the beneficiary and ultimate owner consenting to the bank’s due-diligence process.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Non-resident investors must file a foreign investment notification under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act with a domestic foreign exchange bank or the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy, and then remit funds through a MT103 to the Korean company’s foreign currency capital escrow account at a licensed Korean bank. The remittance should use the standard direct-investment transaction purpose code and include the foreign investment notification number, investor name, and beneficiary name. The receiving bank performs capital verification by matching the remittance to the issued shares and initial constitution; the company must provide board minutes, the investment application, shares allotment statement, and a legal opinion from a Korean counsel. After the deposit is cleared, the bank issues a certificate of foreign-invested enterprise registration, which is necessary for the company to operate and for future dividend remittances.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlement should be routed through the Korean commercial banking system. For direct supplier payments, issue an SWIFT MT103 with the commercial invoice, packing list and import customs declaration, using the seller’s bank details and the correct FEIS purpose code. For large or first-time orders without a supply relationship, open an irrevocable at-sight or deferred commercial Letter of Credit through a domestic Korean bank, with documents consisting of the phytosanitary certificate, certificate of origin, and full set bills of lading. For smaller cross-border purchases, a documentary collection (D/P or D/A) through the issuing bank is permissible. For consumer exports from the ecommerce platform, the rails are dominated by card networks and local PSP settlement, followed by a scheduled aggregate payout via SWIFT into the Korean corporate account; each payout is subject to FX conversion and FEIS reporting.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore KRW/USD deliverable FX forwards with a Korean foreign exchange bank, limited to the notional amount of outstanding trade payables/receivables or the anticipated dividend remittance
Non-deliverable currency swaps and cross-currency interest-rate swaps for the foreign currency project finance portion, provided the underlying is a real cross-border investment debt exposure

KRW NDF transactions with licensed onshore banks to hedge anticipated KRW cash flows from the ecommerce business, executed only for risk-hedging and not for speculative profit, with full documentation of the underlying exposure

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Ordinary General Shareholders Meeting, approval of annual financial statements, and recordation of the meeting minutes in the legal minute book under the Korean Commercial Act
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registered shareholders of the Chusik Hoesa; meeting minutes maintained at the head office and inspected by shareholders; no separate government filing unless foreign-investment reporting is triggered
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the end of the fiscal year; for a calendar-year company, on or before 31 March annually
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to convene the ordinary general meeting or to obtain the required financial statement approval exposes directors and statutory representatives to administrative fines under the Korean Commercial Act, currently up to KRW 5 million (USD 3,650); persistent corporate dysfunction may be used by the National Tax Service or the court as evidence for involuntary dissolution or administrative strike-off proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return, tax base reconciliation, and self-assessment, including any supplementary schedules arising from cross-border nutraceutical sales
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) through the HomeTax electronic filing system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the fiscal year end; for a December year-end entity, by 31 March; one additional month is allowed if the corporation files electronically through HomeTax, giving a final e-filing deadline of 30 April
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers an additional tax equal to 20 percent of the unpaid corporate tax; under-reporting attracts a 10 percent penalty, rising to 40 percent for fraudulent under-reporting; overdue tax accrues daily interest at approximately 0.022 percent from the statutory due date until full settlement. Unpaid tax may result in NTS seizure of bank accounts, attachment of trade receivables, forfeiture of the business registration license, and ultimate administrative strike-off of the corporation from the national business registry.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local corporate income tax surtax return and payment, comprising the 10 percent surtax assessed on the national corporate income tax for the preceding fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: The competent city, county, or provincial local government jurisdiction for the registered head office; filed through the WeTax local tax e-filing system or NTS HomeTax joint collection channel
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within four months after the fiscal year end; for a calendar-year corporation, on or before 30 April annually
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing or under-reporting is subject to an additional tax of 20 percent of the local corporate income tax due; overdue amounts attract monthly overdue interest at 1.2 percent under the Local Tax Collection Act. Continued non-payment permits the local government to seize and auction corporate assets and, in serious cases, to cancel the business registration, producing a functional administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual independent certified audit and audit report, if the Chusik Hoesa is subject to the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, including delivery of the audited financial statements to shareholders and disclosure of the audit report to the financial regulator
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: An independent registered certified public accounting firm; for audit-mandated companies, the audit report is submitted electronically via the Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) DART disclosure system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a calendar-year company, the statutory audit must be completed in time for the ordinary general shareholders meeting held by 31 March; the audit report and audited financial statements are required to be disclosed to FSS within two weeks of the ordinary general meeting, subject to the FSS electronic filing deadlines
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to appoint an external auditor when statutorily required subjects the company to administrative fines and, for responsible officers, personal fines under Article 28 of the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies; defective, false, or omitted audit records can invalidate the financial statements, disqualify dividend distributions, and constitute grounds for court-ordered dissolution or shareholder derivative actions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual foreign-invested enterprise business report and utilization-of-investment statement required for the foreign shareholding present in the Chusik Hoesa
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE) through the Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA) foreign direct investment reporting window
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 90 days after the end of each fiscal year; for a calendar-year foreign-invested enterprise, on or before 31 March annually
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A late or omitted annual business report is subject to an administrative fine of up to KRW 2 million (USD 1,460); material omissions or repeated failures with respect to the foreign investment report may lead to cancellation of the foreign-investment registration under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, loss of FIPA-related tax and investment benefits, and administrative strike-off of the entity.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual compliance confirmation of the online dietary supplement and nutraceutical retail business reporting obligation, including food safety management and tracking-reporting obligations for cross-border and e-commerce sales
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Food and Drug Safety (MFDS), with an accepted filing transmitted to the competent local authority that accepted the original food business report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within 30 days of the close of the fiscal year or within 20 days of any material change in business name, location, representative, product category, or cross-border sales channel; calendar-year operators should complete the annual safety confirmation by 31 January
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file the annual food business safety confirmation or to report material changes triggers corrective orders, suspension of online sales, and administrative fines under the Food Sanitation Act and the Special Act on Imported Food Safety; persistent non-compliance can result in cancellation of the food business license and banning of the legal entity from continued e-commerce trading.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies and its Enforcement Decree, a Chusik Hoesa is compulsorily subject to an annual independent certified public accountant audit if (i) total assets at the end of the immediately preceding business year equal or exceed KRW 12 billion, approximately USD 8.8 million at an exchange rate of 1,365 KRW/USD; (ii) the company is a listed company whose shares trade on the Korea Exchange (KRX/KOSDAQ), irrespective of balance sheet size; or (iii) the company holds a regulated financial institution license. The Korean external audit law does not impose a separate general turnover or headcount threshold for an ordinary unlisted nutraceutical e-commerce stock corporation; however, a foreign-invested company may be contractually obliged to produce certified financial statements by covenant in high-risk merchant account agreements, bank finance agreements, or a KOTRA reporting condition, and an online food business permit may require a CPA-reviewed balance sheet as part of license renewal.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: The Chusik Hoesa must maintain accrual-basis double-entry books in Korean won in accordance with the Korean Commercial Act and the Framework Act on National Taxes. Audited entities, and all listed entities, are required to apply Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS), which are fully aligned with IFRS as issued by the IASB. An eligible non-listed small or medium enterprise may apply Korean Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (K-GAAP) approved by the Korean Accounting Standards Board. For the ISIC 4791 cross-border nutraceutical activity, revenue recognition for online sales and promotions must follow IFRS 15 / K-IFRS 1015, inventory valuation must follow IAS 2 / K-IFRS 1002, and cross-border royalties, licensing, and customs duties must be presented in accordance with IAS 21 / K-IFRS 1021.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: South Korea does not operate a public UBO registration regime for ordinary non-financial Chusik Hoesa entities. The controlling statutory protocol is the 30-day event-based reporting window under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act: any foreign investor or foreign-invested enterprise must report to KOTRA/MOTIE, within 30 days of the event, any transfer, pledge, disposal, capital increase, capital decrease, or change in the underlying beneficial ownership of foreign-invested shares. Annually, the foreign-invested enterprise business report due 90 days after fiscal year end constitutes the functional year-end confirmation of the shareholder register and cumulative foreign ownership percentages. For a non-foreign investor, the shareholder registry must be updated promptly and accurately; the Commercial Act requires the shareholder registry to be recorded, and it must be read together with the ordinary general meeting voting record date, which is typically the date on which the immediate preceding one-month period starts. No separate annual UBO attestation is submitted to the tax authorities or company registry for a pure domestic shareholding chain.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members including full legal names, nationalities, residential or registered addresses, number and classes of shares, and dates of acquisition
Register of Directors including personal identification details, nationality, residence, term of office, and other directorships
Register of Statutory Auditors and audit committee members where such positions exist
Register of Debentures and bond issues, if any debentures have been issued
Register of Charges/Mortgages and security pledges affecting corporate assets, including any registered collateral arrangements
Minute Books containing records of general shareholders meetings, board of directors meetings, and audit committee meetings

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 400 - USD 1,500 per annum for a registered office and corporate secretarial agent arrangement; alternative physical head-office lease in Seoul typically ranges USD 10,000 - USD 40,000 per annum for a small corporation
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 6,000 - USD 18,000 for a small to mid-sized audited Chusik Hoesa; a cross-border nutraceutical e-commerce entity with multi-currency transactions, intercompany arrangements, or high-risk merchant account covenants may expect USD 15,000 - USD 35,000 per certified audit

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 21% top marginal national corporate income tax rate; lower progressive brackets are 9% on taxable income up to KRW 200 million and 19% on taxable income over KRW 200 million up to KRW 20 billion, with an additional 10% local income tax surcharge on each national tax component.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Foreign-invested high-technology businesses in Free Economic Zones may receive a 100% corporate income tax exemption for five years and a 50% exemption for the following two years under the Special Taxation Limitation Act and the Foreign Investment Promotion Act. The R&D tax credit regime permits up to 30% to 50% deductions of qualifying R&D and human resource development expenditure for small and medium enterprises. Patent box technology income transfer credits and equipment investment tax deductions are also available where the qualifying intangible is developed and exploited in Korea.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Primary return: Form No. 1, Corporate Tax Base and Amount Tax Return, with attached schedules, filed through the National Tax Service (NTS) HomeTax electronic portal (www.hometax.go.kr) or at the competent District Tax Office.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filing is due within three months after the end of the fiscal year. For a calendar-year Korean entity, the statutory deadline is 31 March. The deadline is extended to 30 April when the return is prepared by a certified tax accountant under e-filing procedures.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 – Taxpayer Identification and Corporate Registration Number
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the full legal name of the Chusik Hoesa (stock corporation), Business Registration Number (BRN), tax office code, head office address, representative director name, and the fiscal year covered.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: When 50% or more of the voting shares are held by non-residents, attach the Schedule of Foreign-Owned Company. Disclose the ultimate beneficial owner, each non-resident shareholder's treaty residence, foreign tax identification number, shareholding percentage, and the foreign parent entity. The Korean corporation must appoint a domestic tax representative for service of notices if the foreign shareholder cannot receive Korean tax documents directly.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 – Fiscal Year and Filing Classification
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: State the fiscal year start and end dates, whether the return is a final return, preliminary return, or separate/consolidated return, and confirm whether it is a regular, revised, or corrected filing.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Korean legal entity must operate on its own statutory fiscal year under Korean GAAP and maintain records in Korean won. A foreign parent's different fiscal year does not govern the Korean entity. Where cross-border transactions flow from an overseas affiliate, the Korean books must accrue those transactions on the date the control transfers and show the corresponding intercompany payables or receivables.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 – Gross Sales and Business Revenue
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter gross sales from the online retail of dietary supplements and nutraceuticals under ISIC 4791, including ancillary delivery, membership, or digital-service revenue.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Recognise revenue in accordance with Korean KIFRS/K-GAAP revenue recognition rules. Exclude customs duties separately if passed through to the customer. If the Korean entity transfers inventory from a foreign related party to Korean consumers, evaluate whether the foreign related party carries on a Korean permanent establishment through the Korean entity, warehouse, order fulfilment, or customer service. For cross-border e-commerce, the Korean entity must also reconcile the VAT filing treatment with the corporate income tax revenue figure.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: List cost of goods sold, selling, general and administrative expenses, logistics fees, e-commerce platform commissions, royalties, marketing fees, interest expense, and intercompany service charges.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All payments to non-resident related companies, including royalties, procurement fees, digital-marketing fees, logistics charges, and intercompany debt interest, must meet the Korean arm's-length standard under the International Tax Adjustment Act. Add back non-deductible items in the reconciliation, such as corporate income tax, income-tax-attributable penalties, excessive entertainment expenses over the statutory limit, and thinly capitalised interest. Attach a transfer-pricing adjustment schedule if the Korean entity's taxable income was increased under the Transactional Net Margin Method or Profit Split Method.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 – Tax Base After Loss Carryforward
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Compute taxable income after adjusting book net income for non-deductible expenses, tax-exempt income, capital gains adjustments, and unused net-operating-loss carryforwards.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim loss carryforwards only within the Korean statutory ten-year carryforward limit. Treaty reductions on outbound payments do not alter the Korean entity's domestic loss computation. Where the Korean entity has free-zone income sheltered by a tax holiday, separate accounting is required so that exempt income does not erroneously reduce loss carryforwards available against full-tax income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Apply the 9% / 19% / 21% progressive national corporate tax rates to the tax base, compute the 10% local income tax surcharge, and deduct prepayments or tentative returns.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Korean entity is the taxpayer regardless of foreign shareholding. No loss consolidation with overseas group companies is permitted. If the Korean entity has a foreign branch, report branch income under separate line items and apply the foreign-branch income exemption election only where the branch meets the statutory effective-tax-rate and business-activity requirements.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 7 – Tax Credits and Special Deductions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter R&D tax credits, foreign tax credits, employment-promotion credits, and investment tax credits admissible against the computed corporate income tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A foreign tax credit is available to a Korean resident corporation for qualifying foreign taxes paid on foreign-source income; attach the relevant foreign tax returns and evidence of payment. The Korean entity may not claim a domestic tax credit that is reserved for wholly domestic Korean-owned enterprises unless the foreign-invested entity satisfies the same statutory conditions. Tax-holiday credits and treaty foreign-tax credits must be computed on separate floating schedules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 8 – Non-Resident Repatriation and Withholding Declarations
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declare retained earnings available for distribution, actual or deemed dividend distributions to non-residents, interest or royalties remitted abroad, and the amount of Korean withholding tax paid on those cross-border payments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the Korean entity pays dividends to a foreign corporate shareholder or remits royalties/interest to a foreign related party, attach the withholding tax return (national tax and local income tax surcharge) and the Form for DTA rate reduction or refund. Computations must reflect the statutory 22% aggregate withholding rate (20% national plus 2% local surcharge) unless a treaty reduction is supported by a valid Tax Residency Certificate and a beneficial-ownership declaration. A failure to withhold at the appropriate rate makes the Korean entity jointly liable for the unpaid foreign-shareholder tax.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: A failure to file by the statutory deadline attracts a 20% negligence surcharge on the unpaid corporate tax, increasing to 40% for grossly false returns filed with intent to evade. Underpaid tax due to incorrect reporting is subject to a 10% negligence surcharge, or 20% to 40% for fraudulent underreporting. Delinquent tax not paid by the due date is charged a daily surcharge of 0.022%. Criminal sanctions under the Punishment of Tax Evasion Act can reach imprisonment of up to five years and a fine of up to five times the tax evaded where the false return is accompanied by concealment or fraudulent intent.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Supplementary return package: Schedule of Foreign-Owned Company, Transfer Pricing Adjustment Schedule, and Withholding Tax on Nonresidents (R13/24), all filed through the HomeTax system.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual, attached to the main corporate income tax return and withholding tax returns at each remittance date.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: All supporting schedules must be submitted with the main corporate income tax return by the same statutory deadline. Withholding tax on actual dividends, interest, and royalties remitted during the year is due within ten days after the end of the month in which the payment is made.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Schedule A – Foreign Shareholder and UBO Disclosure
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report each foreign shareholder with a minimum ownership interest, treaty country, tax residence, UBO structure, and the percentage of Korean entity ownership.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide full chain-of-ownership documentation before claiming treaty benefits. The Korean entity must retain copies of each foreign shareholder's Tax Residency Certificate, certificate of incorporation, board minutes confirming the dividend or royalty receipt, and evidence that the recipient does not act as a nominee or conduit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Schedule B – Arm's Length Comparables and Intercompany Transactions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: List cross-border related-party transactions by type, amount, pricing methodology, and comparability adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For each intercompany transaction, identify the chosen arm's-length method and attach a comparability study. A Korean entity with revenue above the statutory threshold must submit a Local File, and a Master File where the multinational group prepares one. The Korean entity must also substantiate where the Core Income-Generating Activities are performed; if the substance is in Korea, the related-party booking cannot shift profits offshore.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Schedule C – DTA Relief and Beneficial Ownership Application
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Show the treaty article under which the reduced withholding rate is claimed, together with the statutory 22% withholding computation and the reduced treaty WHT computation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For each repatriation, the Korean entity must file the DTA withholding rate reduction or refund application before payment, or within the refund period, and present: (i) a Tax Residency Certificate issued by the foreign revenue authority; (ii) a beneficial-ownership statement declaring that the recipient is the real owner and exercises full control over the income; (iii) proof that the shareholder owns the required percentage of shares for the duration specified in the treaty; and (iv) where the treaty contains a Limitation on Benefits clause, evidence of the recipient's substantive business activity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Other Schedules – Tax Holidays, R&D Credits, and Foreign Branch Reporting
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report free-zone or subsidiarity tax exemptions, R&D credits, and foreign-branch income details.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A foreign-invested enterprise qualifying for the Free Economic Zone tax holiday must complete the dedicated investment schedule and file annual post-approval reports to the NTS. Tax credits are nonrefundable unless law expressly provides; any carryforward of unutilized credits must be reconciled with the loss-carryforward schedule.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to attach mandatory schedules where the entity exceeds the statutory documentation threshold is treated as an incomplete return and triggers the same 20% negligence surcharge. Failure to submit transfer-pricing documentation on request of the National Tax Service attracts a fine for non-submission under the International Tax Adjustment Act, and a shoddy or false documentation claim is treated as fraudulent underreporting. Withholding tax remittance not made on time is subject to a 0.022% daily delinquency surcharge, joint liability of the Korean payer for the non-resident's tax, and potential criminal sanctions for a willful withholding failure.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 20% national withholding tax plus 2% local income surcharge, producing an aggregate 22% statutory dividend withholding tax on dividends paid to non-resident shareholders.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim a reduced or zero dividend withholding rate under an applicable Double Tax Treaty, the Korean payer or the recipient must file a DTA withdrawal application with the National Tax Service before payment, or apply for a refund within the statutory claim period. The protocol requires a Tax Residency Certificate issued by the foreign tax authority, a signed beneficial-ownership certificate through which the recipient confirms that it is the true owner and not a conduit, evidence of the shareholding percentage and minimum holding period required by the treaty, and, where applicable, a Limitation on Benefits analysis showing substantive economic activity. Without these filings the full statutory 22% withholding must be applied. The Korean entity is jointly liable for the withholding tax if it distributes dividends without complying with the application and reporting requirements.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rates on royalty and interest outbound from Korea are 20% national withholding plus 2% local income surcharge, giving a 22% aggregate rate. Under typical Korean double taxation treaties, royalty and interest rates are often reduced to 10% to 15%, subject to entitlement conditions, beneficial ownership substantiation, and royalty anti-abuse provisions. Hungarian, Irish, and UK treaties may reduce royalty/interest withholding to 0% in specific conditions only when the recipient is the beneficial owner and the transaction is not generated for treaty-shopping purposes.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Korean entities with annual gross sales exceeding KRW 100 billion, or with aggregate cross-border related-party transactions exceeding KRW 50 billion, are required to prepare and submit a Local File and, where the group consolidates, a Master File under the International Tax Adjustment Act. The Country-by-Country Report is mandatory when the multinational consolidated group revenue is at least KRW 1 trillion. High-risk cross-border e-commerce sellers may be required to file transfer-pricing documentation regardless of the general threshold where the NTS issues a documentation request.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea does not apply a full Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) code as in the UAE, but the National Tax Service applies substance-over-form and anti-abuse doctrines under the Framework Act on National Taxes and the International Tax Adjustment Act. The entity claiming treaty benefits must demonstrate genuine economic presence, personnel, and business decision-making. For a Korean supplement entity, Core Income-Generating Activities such as local order fulfilment, Korean customer support, inventory management, local compliance with food and drug registration, and e-commerce platform risk management are attributes that Korean tax authorities treat as Korean sources of profit. A foreign shell holding company with no CIGA will be denied withholding relief, and its interposed transactions may be recharacterised as a sham.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion / Fraudulent Corporate Income Tax Return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Systematic omission of cross-border e-commerce supplement sales, fabrication of import invoices, use of undisclosed high-risk merchant accounts, and overstatement of royalties or digital-marketing fees paid to a related party in a tax haven with no identifiable commercial function.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: This violates the Corporate Tax Act and the Punishment of Tax Evasion Act. The National Tax Service may impose a 20% unfaithful-return surcharge on the underpaid tax, increase the surcharge to 40% for fraudulent returns, and add a daily delinquency surcharge of 0.022%. Criminal conviction may lead to imprisonment of up to five years and a fine of up to five times the evaded tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil is pierced where directors knowingly conceal revenue or fabricate expenses. Directors are jointly and severally liable to restore the evaded corporate tax from personal assets, may be blacklisted for overseas travel, and may face criminal imprisonment. The NTS may attach personal bank accounts and real estate where the director is found to have controlled the fraudulent reporting.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Aggressive Transfer Pricing and Base Erosion Through Royalties
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging non-arm's-length royalties, management fees, or import markups to a foreign related party for intangible property that has no development history, no personnel, and no business risk in the recipient jurisdiction, and filing the Korean return without a comparability study or with a false TNMM analysis.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Articles 5 through 9 of the International Tax Adjustment Act, the NTS may adjust the transaction to the arm's-length price, impose a 20% negligence surcharge on the understated tax, and assess local income tax surcharge. Failure to submit the mandatory Local File and Master File is punishable by a documentary penalty of up to KRW 20 million.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign the transfer-pricing return knowing that it lacks a factual or economic basis are personally exposed to civil restitution orders for the underpaid tax, travel bans under NTS blacklisting procedures, and criminal prosecution for abetting tax evasion. Where the structure is a sham, the director may be de facto taxpayer for the adjusted corporate income, and the foreign asset trail may attach personal liability.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company Abuse, AML UBO Failure, and Treaty Shopping
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a Hong Kong, Delaware, or zero-tax shell corporation as the nominal shareholder or intellectual-property owner solely to obtain a reduced DTA dividend and royalty withholding rate, failing to file UBO disclosures, and processing dietary-supplement merchant receipts through undisclosed high-risk payment accounts that mask the Korean economic activity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The NTS will deny treaty relief under the beneficial-ownership and Limitation on Benefits rules, reapply the 22% statutory withholding, and assess negligence surcharges. The Financial Transaction Reports Act provides for fines of up to KRW 50 million and imprisonment of up to three years for the willful failure to report the ultimate beneficial owner of a high-risk account. Where the criminal proceeds are laundered, the predicate offence can attract imprisonment of up to seven years under Korean anti-money laundering legislation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who orchestrate the shell arrangement are personally liable for the unpaid withholding tax as withholding agents. The corporate veil is pierced for fraud, permitting creditors and the NTS to execute against director assets. Travel bans and blacklisting are imposed where unpaid national tax exceeds the statutory threshold. Criminal conviction can result in imprisonment and confiscation of assets traceable to the tax fraud and money laundering.
